report:
**Conclusion:** The claim that drinking boiled garlic water cures COVID-19 is **false**.

While garlic has general antimicrobial and health-promoting properties due to natural compounds like allicin, there is no scientific or clinical evidence that garlic or garlic water can prevent, treat, or cure COVID-19 (SARS-CoV-2). 

Public health organizations, including the World Health Organization (WHO), and independent fact-checkers have debunked this claim, which originated as a viral social media rumor early in the pandemic. Health experts emphasize that relying on unproven remedies to treat COVID-19 can be dangerous if it delays necessary medical evaluation and proven treatments.

**Sources:**
- FactCheck.org: https://www.factcheck.org/2020/02/fake-coronavirus-cures-part-2-garlic-isnt-a-cure/
- AFP Fact Check: https://factcheck.afp.com/health-experts-refute-false-claims-drinking-boiled-garlic-water-cures-novel-coronavirus
- Africa Check: https://africacheck.org/fact-checks/meta-programme-fact-checks/no-garlic-doesnt-cure-coronavirus-get-covid-19-facts-only
- World Health Organization: https://www.who.int/emergencies/diseases/novel-coronavirus-2019/advice-for-public/myth-busters
